correctness.rationale: For fixed start/reset position x, the cover time is pathwise the maximum of the two first hits, including an endpoint occupied initially. For a target, let φ be its no-reset first-hit Laplace transform at r; a renewal attempt succeeds with probability φ and lasts on average (1−φ)/r, giving mean (1−φ)/(rφ). Solving the Dirichlet/Neumann problems (two Dirichlet conditions for either endpoint) and taking the sum of the two target means minus the either-hit mean gives the stated objective. In z=cosh(sqrt(r/D)(x−L/2)), b=cosh(sqrt(ρ)), the derivative has positive denominator and numerator b F_b(z²); re-expansion gives F_b(y)=(3−4b²)y²+4b²(b²−1)y+(b²−1)². Its roots have opposite signs and its positive root is simple, so only z=1,b can minimize. The difference H_b(1)−H_b(b)=−(b−1)(2b²−b−2)/b gives all ties, locations and the stated minimum. F_b(b²)=1−2b²<0, F_b(1)=5(b²−1)²−1; hence endpoints are always strict one-sided minima and each half gains exactly one maximum when F_b(1)>0. At equality H''_b(1)<0 and z−1 is quadratic in displacement, giving strict quartic flatness. At b_s the crossing polynomial is 2/sqrt(5)−b_s<0, confirming b_s<b_c.
